a.n: Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias
a.d: Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias (pol. Miasteczko Sztuki i Nauki) – kompleks obiektów kulturalno-rozrywkowych w hiszpańskiej Walencji o powierzchni całkowitej 350 000 m², otwarty 16 kwietnia 1998 r., zwany przez mieszkańców miasta „dzielnicą przyszłości”.

a.h: Nov-Mar: Mon-Sat 10:00-17:30; Apr-Oct: Mon-Sat 10:00-18:30, Sun 14:00-18:30; last admission 45 min before closing
a.d: Katedra w Walencji (znana po katalońsku jako „Seu”) – siedziba diecezji miasta Walencja w Hiszpanii. Jest poświęcona Matce Bożej.
a.de: It was the site of a Roman temple, then a Visigothic cathedral, and then a Moorish grand mosque. It is now the seat of the archbishropic of Valencia. The current Gothic structure was begun in 1262 and remodeled numerous times, resulting in a structure with elements from three distinct architectural

a.n: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía
a.d: El Palau de les Arts Reina Sofia (z wal. „Pałac Sztuk Królowa Zofia”; hiszp.
Muzeum Sztuk Pięknych w Walencji (hiszp. Museo de Bellas Artes de Valencia) – mieszczące się w Walencji muzeum sztuki.
a.de: This 17th-century former palace houses over 2,000 pieces of art, with a primary focus on art of the 14th to 17th centuries. Highlights include an excellent collection of medieval altarpieces, a collection of engravings by the Italian artist Piranesi, and a handful of minor works by Velázquez, El Gre

a.d: Hemisfèric – jeden z budynków Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias w Walencji, otwarty 16 kwietnia 1998 roku. Zbudowany został na kształt oka, a zaprojektował go Santiago Calatrava.
Park miejski w dawnym korycie rzeki Turia, ciągnący się na prawie 8,5 kilometra i zajmujący około 136 hektarów. Jest jednym z największych czysto miejskich ogrodów w Hiszpanii.
Muzeum poświęcone tradycyjnej i ludowej kulturze walenckiej. Zbiera, bada i przekazuje materialne oraz niematerialne dziedzictwo regionu.
Historyczny pałac z XV wieku, zbudowany w walenckim gotyku z późniejszymi dodatkami renesansowymi. W 1931 roku uznano go za dobro kultury, a dziś mieści władze wykonawcze wspólnoty.
Gotycki kościół parafialny założony w XIII wieku, przebudowany w stylu gotyku walenckiego w XV wieku. Ma rozetę nawiązującą do cudu świętego Mikołaja.
a.de: Established in the 13th century, the church was expanded in several phases, culminating in the current 15th-century Gothic structure. During the late 17th century extensive Baroque renovations were carried out to the interior, the most significant of them being ceiling frescoes. This remarkable set

The centrepiece of this unusual playground is a 70-m-long sculpture of Gulliver (from the classic book Gulliver's Travels), who has been tied to the ground. Visitors can climb on and slide down the giant figure, much as Lilliputians might have. The sculpture was designed by Valencian artist and illu

a.n: Palau de la Música de València
a.h: 10:30-13:30, 17:30-21:00 (ticket office); tickets can also be purchased [http://www.entradas.com/tickets.html?affiliate=
a.de: Designed by José María de Paredes and opened in 1987, this is considered to be one of Europe's most important concert halls. The building is marked by an enormous glass greenhouse-like structure which also serves as the main entrance. In addition to classical music, jazz concerts are also performed

a.n: Church of Sant Joan del Mercat
a.d: Kościół z połowy XIII wieku wzniesiony na miejscu dawnego meczetu, początkowo w stylu gotyckim. Stoi obok Targu Centralnego, naprzeciw Giełdy Jedwabiu.
Rokokowy pałac szlachecki w jednym z najbardziej centralnych miejsc Walencji, własność państwa. Mieści Narodowe Muzeum Ceramiki i Sztuk Zdobniczych González Martí.
Muzeum Prehistorii w Walencji (hiszp. Museo de Prehistoria de Valencia; ca.
Gotycki kościół przy Plaça de Sant Esteve, jeden z najstarszych w Walencji, zbudowany na miejscu meczetu. Według legendy stała tu wcześniej rzymska świątynia Herkulesa.

a.n: National Museum of Ceramics and Sumptuary Arts González Martí
a.de: This very ornate Baroque palace once served as the residence of the Marqués de Dos Aigües, and is now a museum. The ground and first floors showcase a collection of stagecoaches and period furniture, while the upper two floors house an extensive ceramics collection with a focus on historic Valencian

a.n: Reial Col·legi Seminari de Corpus Christi

a.d: Centralny plac Walencji, na którym zbiega się kilka ulic, z barokowymi Drzwiami Żelaznymi prowadzącymi do katedry. Widać z niego dwie ważne dzwonnice: Santa Catalina i Miguelete.
Zamek-pałac Alaquàs, zamek Czterech Wież lub Pałac Aguilar – rezydenca szlachecka zbudowana w XVI wieku. Znajduje się w Alaquàs (Walencja) w Hiszpanii.

a.n: Plaça de la Mare de Déu
Jardín Botánico de la Universidad de Valencia
a.d: Ogród botaniczny przy calle Quart, w obecnym miejscu od 1802 roku. Uniwersytet uprawiał zioła lecznicze już w XVI wieku, a ogród nadal służy nauce i edukacji.

a.n: Museu de Ciències Naturals de València
a.de: The museum is divided into several segments, covering Valencian contributions to the sciences, the ecology of the Valencian region, and of course paleontology with the requisite dinosaur skeletons.

a.n: El Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe
a.h: Winter Mon-Thu 10:00-18:00, Fri Sat 10:00-19:00; spring/fall and Christmas season daily 10:00-19:00; summer daily 10:00-
a.d: Museo de las Ciencias Príncipe Felipe (pol. Muzeum Nauki Księcia Filipa) – hiszpańskie muzeum poświęcone nowym technologiom, nauce i środowisku naturalnemu, mieszczące się w kompleksie Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias (pol.
a.de: A science museum designed to resemble a whale skeleton, it has interactive exhibits on three floors.

a.d: Oceanarium i morska stacja badawcza w Miasteczku Sztuk i Nauk, otwarte 14 lutego 2003 roku. Zajmuje 110 tysięcy metrów kwadratowych, a wszystkie zbiorniki mieszczą łącznie 42 tysiące metrów sześciennych wody.
Ogród rzeźb i promenada w Miasteczku Sztuki i Nauki, z gatunkami roślin typowymi dla Walencji. Wewnątrz mieści Aleję Rzeźb, plenerową galerię prac współczesnych artystów, między innymi Yoko Ono.
a.de: A botanic garden landscaped with plants native to Valencia. The park also has the Jardí d'Astronomia (Jardín de la Astronomía / Astronomy Garden) and the Passeig de l'Art (Paseo del Arte / Art Promenade), which has permanent and temporary exhibits of large-scale contemporary art, mostly sculpture.
A multi-use covered plaza, designed for sporting events, concerts, and special exhibits.
The striking cable-stayed bridge designed by Santiago Calatrava and completed in 2008, crosses the dry Túria riverbed. At 125 m high, the bridge tower is the highest point in Valencia.

a.d: Dzwonnica katedry w Walencji, zwana też Torre del Micalet, budowana od 1381 do 1429 roku. Z powodu skomplikowanej konstrukcji i długiej budowy kierowało nią kolejno kilku mistrzów budowlanych.
a.de: The focus of this side chapel is a chalice of agate, the top of which is believed by the devout to be none other than the Holy Grail. Of the handful of similar chalices with the same claim, this is deemed by many scholars to be the most likely candidate as that part has been dated by experts to the
The unusual octagonal bell tower, with a height of 51 m, was built in the 14th and 15th centuries. It provides a pleasing view of the city.

a.n: Cripta arqueològica de la presó de Sant Vicent Màrtir
a.de: This Visigothic chapel has on display objects discovered during its excavation including a Visigothic altar, Roman mural, Muslim artifacts, and a sculpture of the early Christian Saint Vicente Mártir, who is believed to have been buried here.

a.d: Giełda Jedwabiu (hiszp. Lonja de la Seda, kat.
a.de: This UNESCO landmark is considered to be one of the most significant secular Gothic buildings in Europe. It was built between 1482 and 1533 on the site of an earlier oil exchange. The Llotja consists of four distinct parts: the Sala de Contractació (Trading Hall), also known as the Saló Columnari (H

a.n: Monestir de Sant Miquel dels Reis
a.h: Tours: Sat Sun and holidays 12:00, 13:00; no reservation required
a.de: Founded in the 16th century, this massive Renaissance building is considered by some historians to be the early model for the more well-known El Escorial near Madrid. In 1835 the monastery was dissolved and came under control of the state; it was used for a time as a school, an asylum, and during th

a.d: Jedna z dwóch zachowanych bram dawnych murów Walencji, zbudowana w latach 1441–1493. Mury noszą ślady kul armatnich i muszkietów z wojny na Półwyspie Iberyjskim.
a.de: This medieval tower was part of the wall that surrounded the old city; the numerous pock-marks are from gun battles during the Spanish War of Independence from the French (1807-1814). Great views of the city can be had from the top.

a.d: Wieże Serranos (hiszp. Torres de Serranos, wal.
a.de: Built in 1392, this gate was also part of the ancient wall and for a time also served as a prison. The gate has been massively renovated and somewhat modernized, but is still interesting. It is across the street from the park. This tower also offers excellent views.

Constructed in the early 14th century on the site of a Moorish palace, the building is essentially Moorish in design and used to function as the municipal granary; its name is derived directly from 'almud' (Arabic: bushel). The building was fully restored in 1996 and is now a venue for temporary art

Although constructed in 1313 after the Christian reconquista, the bathhouse was built in the Arabic style and is considered to be an excellent example of Moorish architecture. It was used continuously as a bathhouse until the 20th century, and is one of the few remaining such structures in Spain. It

These Gothic shipyards date to the early 14th century, and attained their current layout in 1500. Trade ships were built and repaired here, as well as galleys used for defense against Barbary pirates. Later the building was used as a storehouse for salt, and now functions as a venue for temporary ex

Built in the 18th century as the residence of the counts of Cervelló, this palace became the official residence for visiting royalty following the demolition of the Palau Reial de València. The building now houses a museum, the Municipal Archive, and the Serrano Morales Library. On the ground floor

Sant Vicent Ferrer, the principal patron saint of Valencia, was born in this house in 1350. The house was renovated numerous times, and has a chapel, well, and 18th-century ceramic tile panels depicting the life of the saint.
One of the few vestiges from Valencia's Muslim period, the semicircular 11th-century tower was once part of the Muslim city wall. It is now a private dwelling, but can be viewed through a fence.

This extensive site was uncovered in 1985 during preparations for new construction, which was then cancelled. Excavations revealed archeological remains dating from the Moorish, Visigothic, and Roman periods. After completing excavations, the city of Valencia converted the site into an underground m
This 19th-century former hospice was completely refurbished in 1995, and now in addition to hosting two museums it also functions as a cultural centre and venue for special exhibits.

a.n: Museu dels Soldadets de Plom L'Iber
a.de: In an old Gothic palace, this is the world's largest private collection of tin soldiers of about one million pieces. Figures represent periods of Valencian, Spanish, and world history.
Built in 1898 for an infantry regiment, the building now houses a collection of over 3,000 objects, most of them from the 19th and 20th centuries.

a.n: Colegio del Arte Mayor de la Seda
a.de: The Moors introduced silk to Valencia, and it became a major hub of the silk trading route during the Middle Ages and Renaissance. The Valencian silk weavers' guild was established in the late 15th century, and in 1494 acquired this building, which remained the guild's headquarters throughout its hi

a.d: Museo del Patriarca – muzeum sztuki znajdujące się w Walencji w Hiszpanii. Siedzibą muzeum jest Real Colegio Seminario del Corpus Christi.
a.de: Managed by the Seminary of Corpus Christi, this museum has a small collection of paintings from the 16th and 17th centuries, with special highlights including works by Juan de Juanes, El Greco, and early Flemish masters. The collection can only be viewed with a tour, offered in a number of European

The museum is devoted to civics and culture, with special exhibits focused on such topics as graphic design, photography, and cinema. The building and garden were designed by Valencian architect Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra.

This former factory from the 1930s has been transformed into an exhibition space for Spanish contemporary art, with a special focus on photography. The building has an interesting history, as it was used to make industrial pumps, and later during the Spanish Civil War was used by the Republicans as

This was once home to two generations of the Benlliure family, headed by prominent Valencian artist José Benlliure. The early 20th-century residence has been maintained in three distinct sections, including the primary house with original furnishings and artworks, a lovely courtyard and garden, and
The former 19th-century residence is a cultural centre which hosts excellent, well-curated temporary exhibits of contemporary art and photography, by Valencian, Spanish and international artists.
The former convent hosts rotating special exhibits showcasing local history, and historic and contemporary artists from Valencia and outside the region.
This well-preserved 14th-century Gothic palace houses a permanent collection of contemporary Spanish art, with rotating exhibits.

This unique underground gallery has been designed around the remains of a city wall from the Moorish period, complete with arches. The gallery is a venue for temporary exhibits of Spanish and international contemporary art.

The oldest bridge in the city, with the current structure dating to the early 16th century. The two 17th-century sculptures of Valencian saints used to be on another nearby medieval bridge, and were relocated to this bridge in the mid-20th century.

This formal Neoclassical garden was designed in the mid-19th century by Valencian architect Don Monleón for the aristocrat Marqués de San Juan. It was declared a 'National Artistic Garden' and is now maintained by the city of Valencia, which opened it to the public in 1973.

a.d: Zoo otwarte w 2008 roku w korycie Turii, z dużą kolekcją fauny afrykańskiej. Koncepcja Zooimersion polega na zanurzeniu zwiedzających w środowisku zwierząt, a nie odwrotnie.

a.h: Summer: daily 07:30-21:30; winter: Mon-Fri 07:30-20:30, Sat Sun 07:30-21:30
a.de: Established by the Moors in the 13th century as gardens for the royal palace (no longer standing), this pleasant and popular park is the second-largest park in Valencia, after the Turia gardens. The park includes a rose garden, sculpture garden, bicycle track, and aviary. During the summer various f

Established by the Moors, then rebuilt by Christians, this building served as the royal Valencian residence until its demolition in 1810. It was forgotten and then rediscovered in 1986. The partially-excavated site is now surrounded by a fence with informative panels in Valencian, Spanish, and Engli

a.h: Every Thu at noon; it is best to get here no later than 11:30 to secure a good spot
a.d: Trybunał Wodny w Walencji (hiszp. El Tribunal de las Aguas de la Vega de Valencia) – trybunał rozstrzygający kwestie związane z dostępem i wykorzystaniem zasobów wodnych w regionie Walencji na obszarze Vega de Valencia.
a.de: The horta (Spanish: huerta), the fertile region surrounding Valencia, has relied on artificial irrigation since antiquity. The tribunal was developed to mediate disputes between farmers, and is believed to date back to Roman times; it has operated in its current form since the Moorish era. The court

a.h: Mon-Sat 09:00-18:00, Sun and holidays 09:00-14:00; 23 Oct - 01 Nov: daily 09:00-18:00
a.de: In use since 1807, the cemetery has some interesting mausoleums and funerary sculpture and is the final resting place for a number of notable Valencians, including members of the artistic Benlliure family, painter Joaquín Sorolla, and writer Vicente Blasco Ibáñez. For visitors with a smartphone ther

a.h: Daily 10:00-20:30; last lift to the top at 20:00
a.de: The viewpoint is on the rooftop of a private social club, and offers excellent 360° panoramic views of the city.

The monumental sculpture dominating the roundabout was designed by internationally-renowned Valencian artist Manolo Valdés and completed in 2007. It was inspired by the Iberian sculpture Dama de Elche ('Lady of Elche'), which was discovered in Elche and now resides in Madrid's National Archaeologica

Since 1934 ninots (papier-mâché figures) voted as the best of the year have been spared the final flames of the Falles festival. Along with photos and posters, these figures are showcased in a building which has served as a lepers' hospital, barracks, and prison.

a.n: Museu de l'Artista Faller de València
Museo de la Semana Santa Marinera
a.de: This small museum has exhibits explaining the Semana Santa Marinera traditions with costumes, documents, and photographs.

The horse-drawn carriages used in the Corpus Christi parades, known as roques (Spanish: rocas, or 'rocks'), have been stored in this building since the mid-15th century. Eleven carriages are on display, the oldest of which was built between 1373 and 1392. Other items exhibited are costumes and histo

a.h: Box office: Tue-Fri 11:00-13:00 17:00-20:00, Sat and holidays 17:00-20:00
a.de: Valencia's oldest theatre was opened 1832 and has a Rococo interior. It is the venue for a varied program of plays and musicals (in Spanish), modern dance, ballet, and concerts.

a.h: Box office: daily 17:00-21:00, ½ hr before performance
a.de: Built in 1915 by Valencian architect Vicente Rodríguez Martín, the theatre is a venue for plays, musicals, and flamenco performances. Tickets can be purchased online.

a.h: Box office: Tue-Fri 18:00-21:00, Sat Sun 2 hr before every show
a.de: The historic theatre was built in 1928 and mostly showcases local plays and actors, but is also occasionally a venue for dance and especially flamenco performances. Tickets can be purchased online.

This café is an intimate venue for flamenco performances, with well-known dancers and musicians hailing not only from Valencia but from across Spain. On Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays performances begin at 23:00 and last for one hour; on Sunday they begin at 20:00. As shows are very popular, it i

a.h: Exhibitions: Tue-Thu 10:00-22:00, Fri-Sun 10:00-23:30; box office: Tue-Sun 10:00-14:00, 2 hrs before performance
a.de: The cultural centre is a venue for music, theatre and dance performances, and hosts rotating temporary exhibits. It also has an onsite restaurant. Tickets for events can be purchased [http://es.larambleta.com/eventos/entradas online].
Interesting cinema with cafe.
A modern cineplex which shows the latest blockbusters, with both dubbed and original language versions (VOS: versión original subtitulada).
A bullring and artistic monument, it is used for bull fighting and big shows. The stadium holds 12,884 people, and was built between 1850 and 1860 by Valencian architect Sebastián Monleón Estellés.

a.h: Tue-Sat 10:00-19:00, Sun Mon 10:00-14:00; closed 1 Jan, 1 May and 25 Dec
a.d: Arena zbudowana w latach 1850–1859 w stylu neoklasycznym według projektu Sebastiána Monleóna Estellésa. Ma 48 boków i 384 zewnętrzne arkady, wzorowane na rzymskim Koloseum i arenie w Nîmes.
a.de: Has displays illustrating the development of Valencian bullfighting since the 19th century.

a.d: Muzeum nowych technologii, nauki i środowiska, otwarte 13 listopada 2000 roku w Miasteczku Sztuki i Nauki. Wystawy są interaktywne, a motto muzeum brzmi: zabrania się nie dotykać, nie czuć, nie myśleć.
Hala targowa naprzeciw Giełdy Jedwabiu i kościoła Santos Juanes, jedno z głównych dzieł walenckiej secesji. Obecny projekt Alexandre'a Solera Marcha wybrano w konkursie w 1910 roku.
Biały most podwieszany z jednym pylonem w Miasteczku Sztuki i Nauki, ukończony w grudniu 2008 roku. Zaprojektował go Santiago Calatrava, a nazwa oznacza po walencku Tamę Złota.

Chroniony obszar przyrodniczy o powierzchni 21 120 hektarów, około 10 kilometrów na południe od Walencji. Nazwa pochodzi od arabskiego słowa oznaczającego jezioro, a w arabskiej poezji zwano je Zwierciadłem Słońca.
Rzymski teatr u stóp góry zwieńczonej zamkiem, uznany za zabytek w 1896 roku. Zbudowano go w połowie pierwszego wieku z wykorzystaniem zbocza, według planu z czasów cesarza Augusta.
Twierdza nad miastem Sagunto, której dzieje sięgają ponad dwóch tysięcy lat. Zniszczenie iberyjskiej osady przez Hannibala w 219 roku przed naszą erą wywołało drugą wojnę punicką.
Kort do walenckiej pilota, jedyny trinquet, który zachował się w centrum Walencji. Powstał 20 sierpnia 1868 roku przy dworcu Estació del Nord, a rozgrywa się w nim finały ważnych turniejów.
